title: FPGA Board Definition
description: Board definition for the Virtual FPGA Board Simulator

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for IDE autocompletion

clocks.description: Clock sources — either flat Hz values or richer objects

default_clock_hz.description: Default clock frequency in Hz used by the simulator

default_clock_assumed.description: Upstream states no frequency for this board's clock, so default_clock_hz is the sync's fallback rather than upstream data, and the chip says so (U56 D-6). Written only when true.

seven_seg.description: 7-segment display definition, or null if absent

source.description: Provenance tracking for this board definition

peripherals.description: Future: typed peripheral definitions (VGA, audio, ADC, etc.)

port_conventions.description: Future: named presets mapping generic ports to vendor-specific port names

pin.description: FPGA pin assignment for this clock input

is_default.description: True if this is the board's default clock

inverted.description: True if the component uses active-low logic

connector.description: Connector reference as [name, number], or null

color.description: LED color when known -- a named color or a #RRGGBB hex string. Absent means unknown, and the renderer falls back to the theme default. On generated boards it flows from sync-time LED-name heuristics or the cited color registry; custom boards may set it directly (U36).

aliases.description: Other upstream names for this same LED: upstream maps each to this LED's pin, or to one channel of this RGB LED (U56 Phase 6, D-1). The sync draws one LED, keeps the first-declared entry as the component, and lists the rest here; each stays a native port of its own.

name.description: The upstream resource name, as the framework spells it (e.g. 'user_ledr_n', 'led_r')

channel.description: The RGB channel this name drives, when the LED is an RGB site

segment_pins.description: Segment pins in a..g (then dp, if the board wires it here) order. One inner list per digit on a directly-driven display; exactly ONE inner list on a scanned display, whose segment lines are shared across digits and selected by digit_enable_pins.

dp_pins.description: Decimal-point pins, one per digit on a directly-driven display or a single shared pin on a scanned one. Omitted when has_dp is false.

digit_enable_pins.description: Digit-select pins, one per digit, in digit order (0 = rightmost). Present only on a scanned display -- its presence is what says the shared segment_pins are multiplexed.

seven_seg.description: A 7-segment display. The three *_pins fields are optional and exist for the pin map (U53), which binds a design's ports to board resources by pin rather than by name; a board without them simply cannot be targeted that way.

origin.description: Where this definition came from, e.g. 'amaranth-boards' or 'custom'

sync_commit.description: Git commit SHA of the source at sync time

sync_timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this file was generated

reference_url.description: URL to board documentation or vendor page

upstream_class.description: The platform class in upstream_file this board was built from (LiteX: the class the parser selects, usually 'Platform'; Amaranth: the class name). Omitted for files without classes (Digilent XDC). Part of the board's identity with origin, upstream_file and upstream_args (U56 plan §4.1).

upstream_args.description: Effective values of the upstream constructor's version-selecting parameters (variant, revision, board_version, ...) for this board, e.g. {"revision": 2}. Omitted when the constructor has none. Part of the board's identity (U56 plan §4.1).

upstream_status.description: 'orphaned': upstream no longer defines this board. The file is kept, frozen at its last good sync, so designs written for it still run (U56 plan §4.3). Absent for a board upstream still defines.

orphaned_at_commit.description: The upstream commit of the sync that found the board orphaned.

orphaned_at_date.description: The UTC date of the sync that found the board orphaned, which the preview shows (U56 Phase 3).

orphaned_reason.description: Why the board is orphaned: its upstream file is gone; the file no longer defines this identity; or the file defines it with no simulatable I/O.

successor.description: A hint, never an automatic migration: '<source>/<file>.json' of the board that most likely replaces an orphan.

convention_source.description: Provenance for a port_convention block populated from the port-convention registry (docs/port_convention_sources/)

url.description: Canonical constraint-file URL the convention was parsed from

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the fetched source file. The drift check compares this rather than the pinned commit, so an upstream commit that does not touch the cited file is not drift

retrieved.description: Date the source was fetched, e.g. '2026-07-11'

registry_board.description: Board identifier as listed in docs/port_convention_sources/

port_convention.description: Maps generic port names to board-specific names for a known convention

leds_green.description: Secondary (e.g. green) LED bank on boards with two-color LED rows, such as Terasic DE2-115's LEDG

led_banks.description: More LED banks a design may drive besides 'leds', each with its 'channels' map: every other upstream LED name -- aliases of an LED, groups split from a multi-pin resource, other named groups (U56 Phase 6). A design may declare any of them; two declared ports that reach one LED channel are a near-miss naming the shared pin.

leds_rgb.description: 3-pin RGB LED channels as a bank of distinct scalar ports ('names', in (r,g,b) order per LED site, sites ascending — matching the boundary channel layout led(MONO + 3i + c)), e.g. Arty's led0_r/led0_g/led0_b/led1_r/... . 'active_low' covers the whole bank; a board whose RGB polarity is unverified or mixed omits this mapping (verify-or-omit).

source.description: Provenance for a convention populated from the port-convention registry (absent for hand-authored blocks)

naming.description: 'canonical': port names come from the vendor/official source; 'project-derived': names were renamed by a downstream project; 'framework-derived': names come from an HDL-framework platform file (litex/amaranth) auto-derived by the sync parsers (U32). Absent means canonical (the default for existing hand-authored blocks).

names.description: Distinct scalar port names, for boards where this resource isn't one shared vector port (e.g. Nandland Go's o_LED_1..o_LED_4, each a separate std_logic port). When present, alongside or instead of 'name'/'width' (width is redundant with len(names) but may still be set for convenience).

channels.description: Bit k of the bank reaches boundary channel channels[k]: an LED channel (mono LEDs first, then r, g, b per RGB site) or a switch/button index; null where the board has no resource for that bit (U56 Phase 6). Absent means bit k reaches channel k ('leds_rgb': the RGB block's channel k).

style.description: 'packed_vector': one vector spanning all digits; 'individual': one port per digit, e.g. HEX0..n; 'per_segment_scalars': one scalar port per segment per digit, e.g. o_Segment1_A; 'scan': shared segment lines multiplexed via digit_enable — for this style 'name'/'names' describe the SEGMENT side (one shared vector, e.g. Basys 3's seg[6:0], or per-segment scalars, e.g. Nexys 4 DDR's CA..CG) and the digit count is digit_enable.width, unlike 'individual' where names are per-digit ports (U22); 'serial': shift-register driven

dp.description: Shared decimal-point scalar port for the 'scan' style (e.g. Basys 3's 'dp', Nexys 4 DDR's 'DP'); same drive polarity as the segments (active_low). Absent when the source lists no shared dp line.

digit_enable.description: Digit-select/enable strobe used by the 'scan' style; its width is the display's digit count
